items.title: Fleet and Family lighting way for NAS JRB New Orleans through Four Lenses
items.author: PO2 Christopher Spaulding
items.summary: Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base (NAS JRB) New Orleans Fleet and Family Support Center (FFSC) staff attended a Four Lenses workshop on Sept. 15 that guided participants in identifying their personality values and strengths that enhance interpersonal relationships.
items.body:
BELLE CHASSE, La. – The Fleet and Family Support Center (FFSC) is a lighthouse for many families and individuals who call Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base (NAS JRB) New Orleans their haven and harbor. As is the case with any beacon, the light provided by FFSC requires calibration to provide guidance through the unique circumstances that bring individuals to them. One of the tools used in this calibration is the Four Lenses workshop, which the FFSC staff attended Sept. 15 onboard NAS JRB New Orleans.

The purpose of the course is to raise awareness of one’ s inner strengths and values to increase their awareness of the strengths and values of others around them, says Chaplains Religious Enrichment Development Operation (CREDO) Southeast Cmdr. Jim Rutan.

“There isn’t anything you can do to make a team stronger than making a team better understand each other,” said Rutan. “When you understand yourself better, you begin to know what your preferences, strengths and needs are, and you get a window into what other people need as well. This multiplies your strengths”

The course is designed to help individuals learn more about their own personality types to enhance their interpersonal relationships. Adapted from the Meyers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), it simplifies complex personality profiles into four distinct, easy-to-remember color profiles, or “lenses”: gold, orange, green and blue.

According to Four Lenses, blues value relationships and empathetic connections, golds value structure and responsibility, oranges value spontaneity and creativity and greens value logic and systemic planning.

Participants formed groups during the workshop based on their personality types and discussed their values, joys, strengths and needs.

“They’re building a stronger team, a stronger base and stronger command, which makes for a stronger Navy,” said Rutan.

Fleet and Family Support Center Director Lasha George encourages this workshop to any department or tenant command that might seek training for team cohesion and self-awareness.

“When we can take care of ourselves and are full in ourselves, then we can serve others in the capacity that they need us to be present in for them,” said George. “We serve the military community; therefore we want to be present for them and be available. When we are self-aware of who we are and how much we can offer is when we can serve others.”

NAS JRB New Orleans is home to 33 active-duty and Reserve tenant commands from the Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Army and Coast Guard. As a premier military training destination with direct access to Gulf of America airspace, the air station operates two active runways to support joint-force combat readiness and homeland defense missions.
zhParas: 路易斯安那州贝尔蔡斯——舰队与家庭支持中心（FFSC）是许多家庭和个人的灯塔，他们称新奥尔良海军航空站联合预备基地（NAS JRB）为自己的避风港和港湾。正如任何灯塔一样，FFSC 提供的光亮需要校准，以便在将人们带到这里的独特境遇中提供指引。用于这种校准的工具之一是四色镜片工作坊；9 月 15 日，FFSC 工作人员在新奥尔良海军航空站联合预备基地参加了该工作坊。
东南地区随军牧师宗教充实发展行动（CREDO）的 Cmdr. 吉姆·鲁坦（Jim Rutan）表示，该课程的目的是提高人们对自身内在优势和价值观的认识，从而增强他们对周围其他人优势和价值观的认识。
“没有什么比让一个团队更好地相互理解更能增强团队的了，”鲁坦说。“当你更了解自己时，你就会开始知道自己的偏好、优势和需求是什么，也能了解别人需要什么。这会让你的优势成倍增长。”
该课程旨在帮助个人更多地了解自己的性格类型，以增强他们的人际关系。它改编自迈尔斯-布里格斯类型指标（MBTI），将复杂的人格特征简化为四种截然不同、易于记忆的颜色类型，或称“镜片”：金色、橙色、绿色和蓝色。
根据四色镜片理论，蓝色型重视人际关系和共情联结，金色型重视结构和责任，橙色型重视自发性和创造力，绿色型重视逻辑和系统性规划。
在工作坊期间，参与者根据自己的性格类型分组，并讨论各自的价值观、乐趣、优势和需求。
“他们正在打造更强大的团队、更强大的基地和更强大的指挥机构，从而造就一支更强大的海军，”鲁坦说。
舰队与家庭支持中心主任拉莎·乔治（Lasha George）鼓励任何可能寻求团队凝聚力与自我认知培训的部门或驻基地司令部参加该工作坊。
“当我们能照顾好自己、自身充实完整时，才能以他人需要我们陪伴的方式去服务他人，”乔治（George）说。“我们服务军人群体；因此我们希望陪伴在他们身边、随时可用。当我们清楚自己是谁、能提供多少时，才是我们能够服务他人的时候。”
新奥尔良海军航空站联合后备基地驻扎着来自海军、海军陆战队、空军、陆军和海岸警卫队的33个现役和预备役驻站司令部。作为可直接进入美洲湾空域的首屈一指的军事训练目的地，该航空站运营两条现役跑道，以支持联合部队战备与国土防御任务。

items.title: NAVFAC Atlantic awards contract to modernize Norfolk Naval Shipyard electrical infrastructure
items.author: Michael Morris
items.summary: Project P732 will increase electrical capacity and strengthen utility reliability and resilience in support of shipyard modernization and fleet readiness
items.body:
Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Atlantic (NAVFAC Atlantic) awarded a $96.3 million contract Sept. 18 to MEB General Contractors Inc. of Chesapeake, Virginia, for electrical distribution system upgrades at Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth, Virginia.

The contract supports military construction Project P732, Electrical Distribution System Upgrades (Gosport Substation Only), a foundational utility project within the Navy’s Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP). Work is expected to be completed by September 2032.

Project P732 will modernize the Gosport Substation to provide the high-voltage electrical infrastructure needed to support current shipyard operations, planned modernization and future growth. The improvements are designed to increase electrical capacity while strengthening the reliability, resilience and flexibility of the system supporting Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s industrial mission.

“We are very excited to get started on investing in much-needed electrical capacity and resiliency improvements at Norfolk Naval Shipyard,” said Matt Morris, SIOP department director at Norfolk Naval Shipyard. “This project will deliver reliable power to the shipyard to meet both current and evolving fleet needs. This will ensure the shipyard workforce can do what they need to do — maintain and modernize our aircraft carriers and submarines and return them back to the fleet where they belong.”

Reliable, high-capacity electrical power is essential to the complex industrial work performed throughout the shipyard. Dry dock pumps, heavy cranes, industrial machinery, shipboard systems and modernized facilities all depend on consistent, high-quality power. Electrical demand is also increasing as facilities are modernized and newer naval platforms rely more heavily on electricity and electronic systems.

Project P732 will replace obsolete primary transformers and switchgear with modern equipment and connect the upgraded Gosport Substation to the shipyard’s existing electrical distribution system. The improvements are designed to increase electrical capacity while strengthening the reliability and resilience of the infrastructure supporting shipyard operations.

“Project P732 more than doubles the electrical capacity for NSA Portsmouth to support upgraded facilities and new naval platforms,” said Christopher Krus, NAVFAC Atlantic’s Project P732 project manager. “These buildings and ships have an ever-increasing reliance on electricity as legacy steam power is phased out. The project improves reliability and resilience for this critical element of Navy ships’ major maintenance and repair, supporting safe and efficient industrial operations.”

Krus also cited coordination with Dominion Energy Virginia as an important part of improving electrical capacity, power quality, efficiency and controls while upgrading the system to current industry standards and providing flexibility for future growth and expansion.

The project will also modernize the shipyard’s existing supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. The system provides personnel with visibility into electrical distribution and helps them monitor and manage the flow of power. Modernizing SCADA will replace legacy controls and improve the Navy’s ability to oversee and manage the electrical system.

Additional improvements incorporate elevated flood protection and other measures designed to improve the resilience of critical electrical infrastructure against coastal environmental conditions.

Dependable electrical infrastructure directly supports personnel conducting complex maintenance, repair and modernization work. Stable power is necessary for precision tools, heavy industrial equipment, temporary shipboard systems and other capabilities required for production and waterfront operations.

“Resilient shore utilities are the bedrock of naval readiness, powering the dry docks and industrial shops that maintain the nation’s combat fleet,” said Keith R. Barbish, SIOP program director.

Project P732 is part of SIOP, the Navy’s long-term effort to modernize infrastructure at its four public shipyards and ensure they can support the maintenance requirements of the current and future fleet. At Norfolk Naval Shipyard, modernizing foundational utilities provides the capacity and flexibility needed to support improved facilities, advanced industrial capabilities and evolving naval platforms.

Investments in resilient shore infrastructure support the Navy’s ability to maintain and modernize nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and submarines and return them to the fleet. By modernizing the underlying utility systems that enable shipyard operations, Project P732 supports Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s long-term industrial capability, fleet readiness and the Navy’s national defense mission.

Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command is the Navy’s facilities and expeditionary systems command, delivering the planning, design, construction, sustainment and environmental services that support Fleet readiness, warfighter capability and shore infrastructure resilience worldwide.
zhParas: 海军设施工程系统司令部大西洋分部（NAVFAC Atlantic）于9月18日授予位于弗吉尼亚州切萨皮克市的MEB General Contractors Inc.一份价值9630万美元的合同，用于弗吉尼亚州朴茨茅斯市诺福克海军造船厂的配电系统升级。
该合同支持军事建设项目P732——配电系统升级（仅限戈斯波特变电站），这是海军造船厂基础设施优化计划（SIOP）中的一项基础性公用设施项目。工程预计于2032年9月完工。
P732项目将对戈斯波特变电站进行现代化改造，提供支持船厂当前运营、既定现代化改造及未来发展所需的高压电力基础设施。这些改进旨在提高供电容量，同时增强支撑诺福克海军造船厂工业任务的系统的可靠性、韧性和灵活性。
“我们非常高兴能够着手投资于诺福克海军造船厂亟需的电力容量和韧性改进，”诺福克海军造船厂SIOP部门主管Matt Morris（马特·莫里斯）说。“该项目将为船厂提供可靠电力，以满足舰队当前和不断变化的需求。这将确保船厂员工能够完成他们需要做的工作——维护和现代化改造我们的航空母舰和潜艇，并将它们送回所属的舰队。”
可靠的高容量电力对全船厂范围内开展的复杂工业作业至关重要。干船坞水泵、重型起重机、工业机械、舰载系统以及已完成现代化改造的设施，均依赖稳定、高质量的电力。随着设施现代化改造推进以及新型海军平台对电力和电子系统的依赖程度日益提高，用电需求也在不断上升。
P732项目将用现代化设备更换老旧的主变压器和开关设备，并将升级后的戈斯波特变电站接入船厂现有配电系统。这些改进旨在提高供电容量，同时增强支撑船厂运营的基础设施的可靠性和韧性。
“P732项目将使朴茨茅斯海军支援活动（NSA Portsmouth）的电力容量增加一倍以上，以支持升级后的设施和新型海军平台，”NAVFAC Atlantic的P732项目经理Christopher Krus（克里斯托弗·克鲁斯）说。“随着传统的蒸汽动力逐步淘汰，这些建筑和舰船对电力的依赖日益加深。该项目提高了这一海军舰艇大修和修理关键要素的可靠性和韧性，支持安全高效的工业作业。”
Krus还提到，与Dominion Energy Virginia的协调是重要一环，有助于提升电力容量、电能质量、效率和控制系统，同时使系统升级到当前行业标准，并为未来的增长和扩展提供灵活性。
该项目还将对船厂现有的监控与数据采集（SCADA）系统进行现代化改造。该系统使人员能够查看配电情况，并帮助他们监测和管理电力潮流。对 SCADA 进行现代化改造将替换老旧控制系统，并提升海军监管和管理电力系统的能力。
其他改进措施包括抬高防洪设施，以及旨在提升关键电力基础设施对沿海环境条件适应能力的其他措施。
可靠的电力基础设施直接支持人员开展复杂的维护、修理和现代化改造工作。稳定的电力对于精密工具、重型工业设备、临时舰载系统以及生产和水岸作业所需的其他能力至关重要。
“具有韧性的岸上公用设施是海军战备的基石，为维护国家作战舰队的干船坞和工业车间提供电力，”SIOP 项目主任基思·R·巴尔比什（Keith R. Barbish）表示。
P732 项目是 SIOP 的一部分，后者是海军对其四家公共船厂基础设施进行现代化改造的长期努力，旨在确保这些船厂能够满足当前和未来舰队的维护需求。在诺福克海军船厂，对基础公用设施进行现代化改造可提供支持改进设施、先进工业能力和不断演进的海军平台所需的能力与灵活性。
对具有韧性的岸上基础设施进行投资，有助于海军维持和现代化改造核动力航母和潜艇，并使其重返舰队。通过现代化改造支撑船厂运行的基础公用设施系统，P732 项目支持诺福克海军船厂的长期工业能力、舰队战备以及海军的国防使命。
海军设施工程系统司令部是海军的设施与远征系统司令部，负责提供规划、设计、建造、维持和环境服务，以支持全球范围内的舰队战备、作战人员能力和岸上基础设施韧性。

该项目还将对船厂现有的监控与数据采集（SCADA）系统进行现代化改造。该系统使人员能够查看配电情况，并帮助他们监测和管理电力潮流。对 SCADA 进行现代化改造将替换老旧控制系统，并提升海军监管和管理电力系统的能力。

其他改进措施包括抬高防洪设施，以及旨在提升关键电力基础设施对沿海环境条件适应能力的其他措施。

可靠的电力基础设施直接支持人员开展复杂的维护、修理和现代化改造工作。稳定的电力对于精密工具、重型工业设备、临时舰载系统以及生产和水岸作业所需的其他能力至关重要。

“具有韧性的岸上公用设施是海军战备的基石，为维护国家作战舰队的干船坞和工业车间提供电力，”SIOP 项目主任基思·R·巴尔比什（Keith R. Barbish）表示。

P732 项目是 SIOP 的一部分，后者是海军对其四家公共船厂基础设施进行现代化改造的长期努力，旨在确保这些船厂能够满足当前和未来舰队的维护需求。在诺福克海军船厂，对基础公用设施进行现代化改造可提供支持改进设施、先进工业能力和不断演进的海军平台所需的能力与灵活性。

对具有韧性的岸上基础设施进行投资，有助于海军维持和现代化改造核动力航母和潜艇，并使其重返舰队。通过现代化改造支撑船厂运行的基础公用设施系统，P732 项目支持诺福克海军船厂的长期工业能力、舰队战备以及海军的国防使命。

海军设施工程系统司令部是海军的设施与远征系统司令部，负责提供规划、设计、建造、维持和环境服务，以支持全球范围内的舰队战备、作战人员能力和岸上基础设施韧性。

items.title: NSWCPD Summer Hire Showcase Highlights Emerging Talent, Fleet-Focused Innovation
items.author: Steven Infanti
items.summary: Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) summer interns and temporary hires presented the results of weeks of research, engineering, testing, and technical development during the command’s Summer Hire Showcase.
items.body:
Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) summer interns and temporary hires presented the results of weeks of research, engineering, testing, and technical development during the command’s Summer Hire Showcase.

Twenty presentations delivered by 23 summer hires covered work supporting shipboard machinery systems, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, maintenance, electrical power, automation, materials, and personnel safety. The event concluded with an awards ceremony recognizing the presentations that earned the highest scores from a panel of NSWCPD judges.

Unlike the poster sessions of the past, the 2026 showcase placed presenters in front of a live auditorium audience and required them to explain their projects through slide presentations. The revised format gave each presenter approximately 15 minutes to introduce a technical challenge, explain the methods used to address it, share results, and respond to questions from the judges and audience.

“The slide presentation format asked the summer hires to do more than display the results of a project,” said NSWCPD Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Outreach Program Manager Tristan Wolfe, who coordinated the showcase. “They had to decide what information mattered most, build a clear technical narrative, and explain why their contribution could matter to NSWCPD and the fleet.”

The participants represented summer employment and scholarship programs that included the Naval Research Enterprise Internship Program (NREIP); the Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program; the Virtual Institutes for Cyber and Electromagnetic Spectrum Research and Employ (VICEROY) Program; and other NSWCPD summer hiring opportunities.

Throughout the summer, participants worked alongside NSWCPD engineers, scientists, technicians, cybersecurity professionals, and program personnel. Their mentors helped them understand technical requirements, navigate Navy engineering processes, and connect their assignments to broader fleet needs.

“The mentors give the students access to years of technical knowledge, but they also give them room to solve problems and develop their own ideas,” Wolfe said. “The showcase allowed the summer hires to demonstrate how much they learned and how they applied that knowledge during their time at NSWCPD.”

The presentations reflected the range of engineering and fleet support conducted across the command.

Topics included applying artificial intelligence, using machine learning to estimate electrical current from magnetic fields, precision maintenance, superconducting magnetic energy storage, oil substitution compatibility, epoxy pipe patching, machinery control, cybersecurity for hull, mechanical, and electrical operational technology control systems, and the automation of recurring technical processes.

Other presenters discussed an enclosure flooding alert system, personnel safety barriers, emergency switchboard requirements, consolidated wire connection lists, test facility upgrades, shaft speed indication, and automated scanning for multi-program test stands.

Judges evaluated the presentations based on factors that included organization, presentation skills, the stated project objective, technical background, methodology, execution, conclusions, future applications, and the presenters’ responses during the question-and-answer portion. Similar criteria have been used during previous NSWCPD summer internship presentation events.

Justin Quinn and Kirsten Nelson earned first place for their presentation, “Personnel Safety Barriers (PSB).”

This NSWCPD Hull Outfitting and Shipboard Habitability branch team developed a redesign for the DDG 1000-class personnel safety barrier. The manual, mechanical design is intended to improve the barriers’ functionality, safety, and reliability while eliminating dependence on electrical components.

“Winning first place was exciting, but what meant the most was representing the branch and highlighting the combined effort and support behind our project,” said Quinn, an NREIP intern and mechanical engineering student at Penn State University. “During two summers and one fall at NSWCPD, I gained experience in in-service engineering, project management, and other areas that prepared me to accept a full-time position here.”

“Receiving this recognition was a testament to how much I learned from my mentors and projects during my internship,” said Nelson, a SMART Scholar studying mechanical engineering at York College of Pennsylvania. “It was rewarding to share the achievement with my code, my school, and the SMART Scholarship program. I also learned how important standardization is across the fleet, and I’m excited to return to NSWCPD full time after I graduate.”

Elizabeth McCaskey received second place for her “Answer File Automation.” McCaskey, a VICEROY scholar assigned to NSWCPD’s Steam and Ventilation Controls branch, developed an automated solution to streamline the Risk Management Framework. The files fill gaps in scan results by documenting mitigations for open vulnerabilities and adding comments for vulnerabilities that have been closed or determined not applicable.

“Receiving second place showed me that the judges saw value in both the work and the way I presented it,” said McCaskey, who earned a bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity from West Virginia University and is beginning a master’s degree in the same field. “The internship gave me hands-on experience with material I could continue working with for years, and it helped me build connections with people inside and outside my code.”

Third place went to Ryan Dott for “Cybersecurity for Hull, Mechanical & Electrical (HM&E) Operational Technology Control Systems.”

Dott, an NREIP intern assigned to NSWCPD’s Aircraft Vehicle Ship Material Handling branch, examined the implementation of cybersecurity methods for HM&E operational technology control systems. His work allowed him to apply his cybersecurity knowledge to experimental technology while addressing technical challenges involving systems that support Navy operations.

“Placing in the top three was incredibly rewarding because I spent the last 10 weeks researching new cybersecurity methods, learning unfamiliar systems, and working through roadblocks,” said Dott, an electrical engineering student at Clemson University. “The Navy gave me the resources to succeed, and my mentors were always there to guide me through complex technical challenges. The award capped off a summer in which I gained hands-on experience and contributed tangible results to the Navy mission.”

While the awards recognized the highest-scoring presentations, Wolfe emphasized that the showcase represented the culmination of a summer of learning for every participant.

“An award is a meaningful recognition, but the larger success is seeing every presenter stand before an audience and explain how they contributed to a Navy engineering organization,” Wolfe said. “They gained technical experience, learned from NSWCPD mentors, and strengthened the communication skills they will need throughout their careers.”

The showcase also gave NSWCPD employees an opportunity to learn about projects taking place across departments and to meet students who could become part of the Navy’s future science and engineering workforce.

NSWCPD internships pair students with mentors and technical assignments involving areas such as testing and evaluation, modeling and simulation, research and development, cybersecurity, and in-service engineering. Participants complete projects connected to shipboard machinery and supporting systems and present the results at the end of the summer.

For the summer hires, the showcase marked both the conclusion of their assignments and an opportunity to demonstrate how their classroom knowledge could be applied to challenges affecting Navy ships and Sailors.

“These summer programs introduce talented students to the Navy mission, but they also allow us to learn from the energy and new ideas those students bring into the command,” Wolfe said. “The showcase demonstrated what can happen when strong mentoring, technical curiosity, and a real fleet need come together.”

NSWCPD employs about 2,700 civilian engineers, scientists, technicians, and support staff. The team focuses on research and development, testing and evaluation, acquisition support, and in-service and logistics engineering for non-nuclear machinery, ship machinery systems, and related equipment and materials for Navy surface ships and submarines. NSWCPD also serves as the main organization responsible for providing cybersecurity for all ship systems.
zhParas: 海军水面战中心费城分部（NSWCPD）的暑期实习生和临时雇员在该中心的“夏季雇员展示会”上，展示了数周研究、工程、测试和技术开发工作的成果。
23名暑期雇员作了20场报告，内容涵盖支持舰载机械系统、人工智能、网络安全、维护、电力、自动化、材料和人员安全的工作。活动最后举行颁奖仪式，表彰获得NSWCPD评委小组最高评分的报告。
与以往的墙报展示不同，2026年展示会要求展示者面对礼堂现场观众，并通过幻灯片演示来解释他们的项目。修改后的形式给每位展示者约15分钟，用于介绍技术难题、解释所采用的解决方法、分享结果，并回答评委和观众的问题。
“幻灯片演示形式要求暑期雇员做的不仅仅是展示项目结果，”协调此次展示活动的NSWCPD科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）推广项目经理特里斯坦·沃尔夫（Tristan Wolfe）说。“他们必须判断哪些信息最重要，构建清晰的技术叙述，并解释他们的贡献为何可能对NSWCPD和舰队有意义。”
参与者来自暑期就业和奖学金项目，包括海军研究事业实习计划（NREIP）、“科学、数学和研究转型（SMART）服务奖学金计划”、网络与电磁频谱研究与就业虚拟研究所（VICEROY）计划，以及NSWCPD的其他夏季招聘机会。
整个夏季，参与者与NSWCPD的工程师、科学家、技术人员、网络安全专业人员和项目人员一起工作。他们的导师帮助他们理解技术要求，熟悉海军工程流程，并将他们的任务与舰队更广泛的需求联系起来。
“导师们让学生接触到多年积累的技术知识，但也给他们解决问题的空间并形成自己的想法，”沃尔夫说。“此次展示让暑期雇员能够展示他们学到了多少，以及他们在NSWCPD期间如何应用这些知识。”
展示内容反映了整个中心所开展的工程和舰队支持工作的范围。
议题包括应用人工智能、利用机器学习从磁场估算电流、精密维护、超导磁储能、油料替代兼容性、环氧树脂管道修补、机械控制、针对船体、机械和电气运营技术控制系统的网络安全，以及重复性技术流程的自动化。
其他演讲者讨论了封闭空间进水警报系统、人员安全屏障、应急配电板要求、综合接线清单、试验设施升级、轴转速指示，以及多项目试验台的自动扫描。
评委根据多种因素对演讲进行评估，包括组织性、演讲技巧、所述项目目标、技术背景、方法、执行、结论、未来应用，以及演讲者在问答环节的回答。此前的NSWCPD夏季实习演讲活动也采用了类似标准。
贾斯汀·奎因（Justin Quinn）和柯尔斯滕·纳尔逊（Kirsten Nelson）凭借其演讲“人员安全屏障（PSB）”获得第一名。
这个NSWCPD船体舾装与舰上居住性科室团队为DDG 1000级人员安全屏障开发了一项重新设计。该手动机械设计旨在提高屏障的功能性、安全性和可靠性，同时消除对电气部件的依赖。
“获得第一名令人兴奋，但最重要的是代表这个科室，并突出我们项目背后的共同努力与支持，”NREIP实习生、宾夕法尼亚州立大学机械工程专业学生奎因说。“在NSWCPD的两个暑期和一个秋季里，我获得了在役工程、项目管理及其他领域的经验，这些经验让我准备好在这里接受一个全职职位。”
“获得这一认可证明了我在实习期间从导师和项目中学到了多少，”纳尔逊说，她是一名SMART奖学金学者，在宾夕法尼亚州约克学院学习机械工程。“能与我的科室、我的学校和SMART奖学金项目分享这一成就，很有收获。我还了解到标准化在整个舰队中多么重要，我期待毕业后全职回到NSWCPD。”
伊丽莎白·麦卡斯基（Elizabeth McCaskey）凭借其“答案文件自动化”获得第二名。被分配到NSWCPD蒸汽与通风控制科室的VICEROY学者麦卡斯基开发了一种自动化解决方案，以简化风险管理框架。这些文件通过记录未解决漏洞的缓解措施，并为已关闭或确定不适用的漏洞添加注释，填补了扫描结果中的空白。
“获得第二名让我看到，评委既看重这项工作本身，也看重我呈现它的方式，”麦卡斯基（McCaskey）说。他拥有西弗吉尼亚大学网络安全专业学士学位，目前正在攻读同一领域的硕士学位。“这次实习让我获得了对今后多年都能持续钻研的内容的实操经验，也帮助我与代码工作内外的人建立了联系。”
第三名由瑞安·多特（Ryan Dott）获得，其课题为“面向船体、机械与电气（HM&E）操作技术控制系统的网络安全”。
多特是分配到 NSWCPD 飞机与舰船物资搬运部门的 NREIP 实习生，他研究了 HM&E 操作技术控制系统的网络安全方法实施情况。他的工作使他得以将网络安全知识应用于实验性技术，同时应对涉及支撑海军作战的系统的技术挑战。
“进入前三名让我感到无比欣慰，因为过去 10 周我一直在研究新的网络安全方法、学习陌生的系统，并设法突破各种障碍，”多特说，他是克莱姆森大学电气工程专业学生。“海军为我提供了取得成功的资源，我的导师也始终在指导我应对复杂的技术挑战。这个奖项为这个夏天画上句号——在这个夏天里，我获得了实操经验，并为海军使命贡献了实实在在的成果。”
虽然这些奖项表彰的是得分最高的演示，但沃尔夫（Wolfe）强调，此次展示会代表着每一位参与者一个夏天学习成果的集中呈现。
“奖项是一种有意义的认可，但更大的成功在于看到每一位演示者站在观众面前，讲述他们如何为海军的一个工程机构作出贡献，”沃尔夫说。“他们获得了技术经验，从 NSWCPD 的导师那里学到了东西，并强化了职业生涯中始终需要的沟通技能。”
此次展示会也让 NSWCPD 的员工有机会了解各部门正在开展的项目，并结识可能成为海军未来科学与工程人才队伍一员的学生。
NSWCPD 的实习项目将学生与导师配对，并安排测试与评估、建模与仿真、研究与开发、网络安全、在役工程等领域的技术任务。参与者完成与舰载机械及配套系统相关的项目，并在夏季结束时展示成果。
对暑期受聘人员而言，这次展示既标志着他们工作任务的结束，也提供了一个展示其课堂知识如何应用于影响海军舰艇和水兵所面临挑战的机会。
“这些暑期项目让优秀学生了解海军使命，但也让我们能够从这些学生为该司令部带来的活力和新想法中学习，”沃尔夫（Wolfe）说。“这次展示表明，当有力的指导、技术好奇心和真实的舰队需求结合在一起时，能够产生怎样的成果。”
NSWCPD 雇用了约 2700 名文职工程师、科学家、技术人员和保障人员。该团队专注于研发、测试与评估、采办支持，以及为海军水面舰艇和潜艇的非核机械、舰船机械系统及相关设备和材料提供在役与后勤工程支持。NSWCPD 还是负责为所有舰船系统提供网络安全的牵头机构。

“获得这一认可证明了我在实习期间从导师和项目中学到了多少，”纳尔逊说，她是一名SMART奖学金学者，在宾夕法尼亚州约克学院学习机械工程。“能与我的科室、我的学校和SMART奖学金项目分享这一成就，很有收获。我还了解到标准化在整个舰队中多么重要，我期待毕业后全职回到NSWCPD。”

伊丽莎白·麦卡斯基（Elizabeth McCaskey）凭借其“答案文件自动化”获得第二名。被分配到NSWCPD蒸汽与通风控制科室的VICEROY学者麦卡斯基开发了一种自动化解决方案，以简化风险管理框架。这些文件通过记录未解决漏洞的缓解措施，并为已关闭或确定不适用的漏洞添加注释，填补了扫描结果中的空白。

“获得第二名让我看到，评委既看重这项工作本身，也看重我呈现它的方式，”麦卡斯基（McCaskey）说。他拥有西弗吉尼亚大学网络安全专业学士学位，目前正在攻读同一领域的硕士学位。“这次实习让我获得了对今后多年都能持续钻研的内容的实操经验，也帮助我与代码工作内外的人建立了联系。”

第三名由瑞安·多特（Ryan Dott）获得，其课题为“面向船体、机械与电气（HM&E）操作技术控制系统的网络安全”。

多特是分配到 NSWCPD 飞机与舰船物资搬运部门的 NREIP 实习生，他研究了 HM&E 操作技术控制系统的网络安全方法实施情况。他的工作使他得以将网络安全知识应用于实验性技术，同时应对涉及支撑海军作战的系统的技术挑战。

“进入前三名让我感到无比欣慰，因为过去 10 周我一直在研究新的网络安全方法、学习陌生的系统，并设法突破各种障碍，”多特说，他是克莱姆森大学电气工程专业学生。“海军为我提供了取得成功的资源，我的导师也始终在指导我应对复杂的技术挑战。这个奖项为这个夏天画上句号——在这个夏天里，我获得了实操经验，并为海军使命贡献了实实在在的成果。”

虽然这些奖项表彰的是得分最高的演示，但沃尔夫（Wolfe）强调，此次展示会代表着每一位参与者一个夏天学习成果的集中呈现。

“奖项是一种有意义的认可，但更大的成功在于看到每一位演示者站在观众面前，讲述他们如何为海军的一个工程机构作出贡献，”沃尔夫说。“他们获得了技术经验，从 NSWCPD 的导师那里学到了东西，并强化了职业生涯中始终需要的沟通技能。”

此次展示会也让 NSWCPD 的员工有机会了解各部门正在开展的项目，并结识可能成为海军未来科学与工程人才队伍一员的学生。

NSWCPD 的实习项目将学生与导师配对，并安排测试与评估、建模与仿真、研究与开发、网络安全、在役工程等领域的技术任务。参与者完成与舰载机械及配套系统相关的项目，并在夏季结束时展示成果。

对暑期受聘人员而言，这次展示既标志着他们工作任务的结束，也提供了一个展示其课堂知识如何应用于影响海军舰艇和水兵所面临挑战的机会。

“这些暑期项目让优秀学生了解海军使命，但也让我们能够从这些学生为该司令部带来的活力和新想法中学习，”沃尔夫（Wolfe）说。“这次展示表明，当有力的指导、技术好奇心和真实的舰队需求结合在一起时，能够产生怎样的成果。”

NSWCPD 雇用了约 2700 名文职工程师、科学家、技术人员和保障人员。该团队专注于研发、测试与评估、采办支持，以及为海军水面舰艇和潜艇的非核机械、舰船机械系统及相关设备和材料提供在役与后勤工程支持。NSWCPD 还是负责为所有舰船系统提供网络安全的牵头机构。

items.body:
A U.S. Marine Corps KC-130J Super Hercules pilot with Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 352, Marine Aircraft Group (MAG) 11, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing observes his surroundings while flying above California, Oct. 17, 2022. The KC-130 is a multi-role, multi-mission tactical tanker and transport aircraft which provides in-flight refueling to fixed wing, rotary wing, and tiltrotor aircraft, as well as rapid ground refueling when required. MAG 11 generates, embarks, and integrates relevant, combat ready aviation forces capable of providing Offensive Air Support, Anti-Aircraft Warfare, Assault Support, Aerial Reconnaissance, and terminal area Control of Aircraft, all in order to ensure success in combat in support of the Marine Air-Ground Task Force and Combatant Commanders. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Jackson Rush)

U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Felix Lopez, a parachute rigger deployed with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, pilots a PS-2 parachute during bilateral free-fall operations in Bizerte, Tunisia, Sept. 21, 2026. This military free-fall training enhanced airborne crisis-response capabilities and reinforced our enduring security partnership with Tunisia to strengthen collaborative cooperation and increase operational readiness with the African nation. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Isaac Garza)

U.S. Marines with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, and Tunisian Special Operations Maritime Task Group members fast-rope from a Tunisian UH-60M Black Hawk for visit, board, search and seizure training during exercise Phoenix Express 2026 in Bizerte, Tunisia, Sept. 16, 2026. Phoenix Express 2026 is a multinational maritime exercise sponsored by U.S. Africa Command and led by U.S. 6th Fleet under U.S. Naval Forces Africa, bringing together North African, European and U.S. maritime forces as part of a global network of navies to enhance cooperation and expertise in maritime security operations in the southern Mediterranean Sea. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Noah Masog)

The Mobile All-Domain Observation and Sensing System (MA-DOSS) prototype supports Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 in coordination with the Provost Marshall’s Office Aug. 19, 2026, during a live-fire exercise. This new capability quietly demonstrated how the Marine Corps is adapting the rules of expeditionary force protection. (PAE Marine Corps photo by Helena Yared)

U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Jerron Cly, a rifleman assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, prepares to fire a multi-role, anti-armor, anti-personnel, weapon system during a heavy explosive weapons range for a live-fire basic skills package at Marine Corps Base Hawaii, Sept. 2, 2026. The live-fire training focused on combat readiness and small-unit leadership through long and short-bay drills, fragmentation grenade employment, and a heavy explosive weapons package, developing 3rd LCT’s team leaders’ ability to employ Marines and make sound decisions in a dynamic combat environment. Cly is from New Mexico. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Iyer Ramakrishna)

MARINE CORPS AIR GROUND COMBAT CENTER TWENTYNINE PALMS, Calif. - During a live-fire exercise in support of Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 in coordination with the Provost Marshal’s Office Aug. 19, 2026, a new capability quietly demonstrated how the Marine Corps is adapting the rules of expeditionary force protection.

U.S. Marines with 3rd Battalion, 2nd Marines, Littoral Combat Force 24, fire a M224 60mm mortar system during a live-fire range at Camp Santiago Joint Training Center, Puerto Rico, Sept. 2, 2026. U.S. military forces are deployed to the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility in support of Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere, Department of War-directed operations, and the President's priorities to disrupt illicit drug trafficking, deter malign actors and protect the homeland through continuous presence. (U.S. Marine Corps photo)

U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. James Brooks, an infantry rifleman, and U.S. Navy Petty Officer 3rd Class Valeria Carmona, a hospital corpsman, both with the 1st Battalion, 6th Marine Regiment, 2nd Marine Division, assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border (JTF-SB) in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, pose for a photo after being awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal near Campo, California, Aug. 15, 2026. Brooks and Carmona were presented with the award for saving the life of an suspected illegal alien that was suffering from a heat-related illness. U.S. Northern Command is working side-by-side with the Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection within narrowly defined authorities to provide unique military capabilities to protect the territorial integrity of the U.S. southern border. (Dept. of War photo by Sgt. Nathan Hislop)

A Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal sits on the collar of U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. James Brooks, an infantry rifleman, with the 1st Battalion, 6th Marine Regiment, 2nd Marine Division, assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border (JTF-SB) in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, the medal was presented during an award ceremony near Campo, California, Aug. 15, 2026. Brooks was presented with the award for saving the life of a suspected illegal alien that was suffering from a heat-related illness. U.S. Northern Command is working side-by-side with the Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection within narrowly defined authorities to provide unique military capabilities to protect the territorial integrity of the U.S. southern border. (Dept. of War photo by Sgt. Nathan Hislop)

U.S. Marines with Golf Company, 2nd Battalion, 1st Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, fire an M3E1 multipurpose anti-armor anti-personnel weapon system during a platoon-level urban assault as part of Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 at Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, California, Sept. 1, 2026. SLTE is designed to be a challenging, realistic training exercise that produces combat-ready forces capable of operating as an integrated Marine Air-Ground Task Force across all domains of military operations. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Vincent Needham)

U.S. Marine Corps light armored vehicles assigned to the 4th Light Armored Reconnaissance Battalion, 4th Marine Division, Marine Forces Reserve, conduct a convoy during a Reserve Mobilization Exercise, Maryland, June 29, 2026. The week-long exercise validates the battalion's ability to rapidly activate personnel and equipment, ensuring the unit can deliver ready forces in response to a national crisis.

A U.S. Marine with Maritime Raid Force, 26th Marine Expeditionary Unit, parachutes into a drop zone during a military freefall sustainment at Raeford, North Carolina, Sept. 3, 2026. Military freefall sustainments are necessary to conduct parachute operations in support of the 26th MEU’s upcoming deployment. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Osmar VasquezHernandez)

U.S. Marines assigned to 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, detect and track simulated adversary forces during a sensing expeditionary advanced base training mission at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, Aug. 22, 2026. The 13th MEU and the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group are underway and conducting routine operations in the U.S. 3rd Fleet area of operations to enhance their combined Navy-Marine Corps readiness and lethality. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Martha Linares)

A U.S. Marine Corps MV-22B Osprey assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced), 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, transits to the forward arming and refueling point at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, Aug. 22, 2026. The 13th MEU and the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group are underway and conducting routine operations in the U.S. 3rd Fleet area of operations to enhance their combined Navy-Marine Corps readiness and lethality. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Martha Linares)

U.S. Marine Corps Joint Light Tactical Vehicles, a Strikemaster mobile anti-ship missile system, and a Norwegian Army National Manoeuvre Air Defence System displace across austere terrain while under tactical escort by Norwegian Home Guard soldiers with 3rd Platoon, District 11, in Jan Mayen, Norway, Aug. 30, 2026. The displacement and interoperability assessment, conducted during Operation Atlantic City 26, evaluated combined command, control, and multi-domain connectivity to ensure NATO can rapidly coordinate layered fires and air defense across contested environments in the High North. Atlantic City 26 is a Norwegian-led trilateral readiness initiative with the United Kingdom and United States designed to develop and demonstrate expeditionary advanced base capabilities and validate combined fires, maritime domain awareness, and sea denial to reinforce the security and stability of the High North. Jan Mayen is sovereign Norwegian territory in an isolated part of the Norwegian Sea, approximately 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from mainland Norway. At the same time, the island occupies an important geostrategic position north of the Greenland-Iceland-U.K. gap, an area of water strategically significant to the defense of the U.S. homeland and northern Europe. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Noah Masog)

U.S. Marines with Echo Company, 2nd Battalion, 1st Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, maneuver to a building during a platoon-level urban assault as part of Service Level Training 4-26 at Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, California, Aug. 30, 2026. SLTE is designed to be a challenging, realistic training exercise that produces combat-ready forces capable of operating as an integrated Marine Air-Ground Task Force across all domains of military operations. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Journey Fisher)

U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. James Martin, a squad leader with Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, fires an M4 carbine during a live-fire range as part of a platoon exchange at the Indonesian Marine Corps 9th Battalion near Lampung, Indonesia, Aug. 21, 2026. This year’s iteration of the annual platoon exchange is between MRF-D and the Indonesian Armed Forces 7th Infantry Battalion, 4th Brigade, designed to enhance combined combat readiness, strengthen tactical interoperability, and reinforce the enduring partnership between both nations. Martin is a native of California. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Kyle Chan)

U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Brandon Anthony, a senior drill instructor with Sierra Company, Support Battalion, Recruit Training Regiment, waits to report to the series commander during pick up on Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, S.C., Aug. 22, 2026. Pick up is when recruits meet the drill instructors who will be responsible for training and mentoring them during the 13-week recruit training. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Jordy Morales)

U.S. Marines with Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, Indonesian marines with 7th Infantry Battalion, 4th Infantry Brigade, Republic of Korea marines with 3rd Reconnaissance Battalion, 6th Marine Brigade, and Japan Ground Self-Defense Force service members with 2nd Amphibious Rapid Deployment Regiment, Amphibious Rapid Deployment Brigade, stand at attention during an opening ceremony for Exercise Super Garuda Shield 26 at the Indonesian Marine Corps 7th Infantry Battalion base near Lampung, Indonesia, Aug. 31, 2026. Super Garuda Shield is an annual exercise between the Indonesian National Armed Forces and U.S. Military designed to strengthen bilateral interoperability, capabilities, and cooperation. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Kyle Chan)

zhParas: 2022年10月17日，美国海军陆战队第3航空联队第11航空大队（MAG 11）第352海军陆战队空中加油运输中队（VMGR 352）的一名KC-130J Super Hercules飞行员在加利福尼亚上空飞行时观察周围情况。KC-130是一种多用途、多任务战术加油机和运输机，可为固定翼、旋翼和倾转旋翼飞机提供空中加油，并可在需要时进行快速地面加油。MAG 11 生成、搭载并整合相关的、做好战斗准备的航空力量，能够提供进攻性空中支援、防空作战、突击支援、空中侦察以及飞机终端区控制，以确保在支持海军陆战队空地特遣部队和作战司令部司令的战斗中取得成功。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. Jackson Rush 拍摄）

2026年9月21日，在突尼斯比塞大举行的双边自由落体行动中，美国海军陆战队 Staff Sgt. Felix Lopez（费利克斯·洛佩斯）——一名随第2海军陆战师第2侦察营部队侦察连部署的降落伞检修员——操控一具PS-2降落伞。此次军事自由落体训练增强了空降危机响应能力，并巩固了美国与突尼斯持久的安全伙伴关系，以加强与这个非洲国家的协作合作并提高作战战备水平。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. Isaac Garza 拍摄）

2026年9月16日，在突尼斯比塞大举行的“Phoenix Express 2026”演习期间，美国海军陆战队第2海军陆战师第2侦察营部队侦察连的陆战队员与突尼斯特种作战海上任务组成员从一架突尼斯UH-60M Black Hawk上快速滑降，进行登临、检查、搜查和扣押训练。Phoenix Express 2026 是由美国非洲司令部主办、由美国驻非洲海军部队下属美国第6舰队领导的多国海上演习，汇集北非、欧洲和美国海上力量，作为全球海军网络的一部分，以加强在地中海南部海上安全行动中的合作与专业技能。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. Noah Masog 拍摄）
2026年8月19日，在一次实弹演习中，移动全领域观察与感知系统（MA-DOSS）原型机与宪兵主任办公室协调，为4-26军种级训练演习提供支持。这项新能力悄然展示了海军陆战队如何调整远征部队防护规则。（PAE 美国海军陆战队照片，由 Helena Yared 拍摄）

2026年9月2日，在夏威夷海军陆战队基地，美国海军陆战队第3海军陆战师第3海军陆战队濒海团第3濒海作战队的步枪手、Lance Cpl. Jerron Cly（杰伦·克莱）在一次重型爆炸武器射击场中为实弹基本技能训练包做准备，准备发射一种多用途、反装甲、反人员武器系统。此次实弹训练侧重于通过长距和短距靶道演练、破片手榴弹使用以及重型爆炸武器训练包来提升战斗战备和小分队领导力，培养第3濒海作战队队长部署陆战队员并在动态作战环境中作出正确决策的能力。克莱来自新墨西哥州。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. Iyer Ramakrishna 拍摄）
加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心——2026年8月19日，在一次与宪兵主任办公室协调、为4-26军种级训练演习提供支持的实弹演习中，一项新能力悄然展示了海军陆战队如何调整远征部队防护规则。
2026年9月2日，在波多黎各圣地亚哥营联合训练中心的一次实弹射击场，美国海军陆战队第2海军陆战团第3营、濒海作战部队24的陆战队员发射一套M224 60mm迫击炮系统。美国军事力量部署到美国南方司令部责任区，以支持西半球联合特遣部队、战争部主导的行动，以及总统的优先事项——通过持续存在破坏非法毒品贩运、威慑恶意行为者并保护本土。（美国海军陆战队照片）

2026年8月15日，在加利福尼亚州坎波附近，美国海军陆战队 Lance Cpl. James Brooks（詹姆斯·布鲁克斯）——一名步兵步枪手——和美国海军 Petty Officer 3rd Class Valeria Carmona（瓦莱里娅·卡莫纳）——一名海军医护兵——在获得海军与海军陆战队成就奖章后合影。两人均隶属于第2海军陆战师第6海军陆战团第1营，被分配到南部边境联合特遣部队（JTF-SB），支持“Ardent Vanguard”行动。布鲁克斯和卡莫纳因挽救一名当时正患高温相关疾病的疑似非法外侨的生命而获奖。美国北方司令部正在狭义界定的权限内，与国土安全部和美国海关与边境保护局并肩合作，提供独特的军事能力，以保护美国南部边境的领土完整。（战争部照片，由 Sgt. Nathan Hislop 拍摄）

隶属于海军陆战队预备役部队第4海军陆战师第4轻型装甲侦察营的美国海军陆战队轻型装甲车，于2026年6月29日在马里兰州举行的一场预备役动员演习中执行车队机动。这场为期一周的演习验证了该营快速动员人员和装备的能力，确保该部队能够响应国家危机投送战备部队。

隶属于第13海军陆战队远征分队的美国海军陆战队员，在2026年8月22日于加利福尼亚州海军陆战队彭德尔顿基地举行的感知远征前进基地训练任务中，探测并跟踪模拟敌军部队。第13 MEU 与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升海军-海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第1师第1陆战团第2营E连的海军陆战队员，在2026年8月30日于加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心举行的军种级训练4-26中，作为排级城市突击的一部分，机动至一栋建筑。SLTE 旨在成为一项具有挑战性、逼真的训练演习，打造能够作为一体化海军陆战队空地特遣部队在所有军事行动领域中作战的战备部队。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 朱尼·费舍尔（Journey Fisher）拍摄）

2026年8月21日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近印度尼西亚海军陆战队第9营举行的排级交流活动中，美国海军陆战队“达尔文轮换部队26”第5海军陆战团第1营A连班长 Sgt. 詹姆斯·马丁（James Martin）在实弹射击场使用 M4 卡宾枪射击。今年的年度排级交流在 MRF-D 与印度尼西亚武装部队第4旅第7步兵营之间进行，旨在提升联合战斗战备、强化战术互操作性，并巩固两国之间持久的伙伴关系。马丁是加利福尼亚州人。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

Jackson Rush 拍摄）

隶属于第13海军陆战队远征分队的美国海军陆战队员，在2026年8月22日于加利福尼亚州海军陆战队彭德尔顿基地举行的感知远征前进基地训练任务中，探测并跟踪模拟敌军部队。第13 MEU 与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升海军-海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

一架隶属于第13海军陆战队远征分队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队（VMM）364（加强）的美国海军陆战队 MV-22B Osprey，于2026年8月22日转场至加利福尼亚州海军陆战队彭德尔顿基地的前沿武装与加油点。第13 MEU 与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升海军-海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队的 Joint Light Tactical Vehicles、一套 Strikemaster 机动反舰导弹系统和一套挪威陆军国家机动防空系统，在挪威扬马延的荒凉地形上进行转移，同时由挪威国土警卫队第11区第3排士兵提供战术护送，2026年8月30日。在“大西洋城26”行动期间进行的转移与互操作性评估，检验了联合指挥、控制及多域连通能力，以确保北约能够在高北地区的争议环境中迅速协调分层火力与防空。“大西洋城26”是挪威主导、英国和美国参与的三边战备倡议，旨在发展和展示远征前进基地能力，并验证联合火力、海域态势感知和海上拒止，以加强高北地区的安全与稳定。扬马延是挪威主权领土，位于挪威海一处偏远海域，距挪威大陆约 1,000 kilometers (620 miles)。同时，该岛占据格陵兰-冰岛-英国缺口以北的重要地缘战略位置，这一水域对美国本土和北欧防御具有重要战略意义。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 诺亚·马索格（Noah Masog）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第1师第1陆战团第2营E连的海军陆战队员，在2026年8月30日于加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心举行的军种级训练4-26中，作为排级城市突击的一部分，机动至一栋建筑。SLTE 旨在成为一项具有挑战性、逼真的训练演习，打造能够作为一体化海军陆战队空地特遣部队在所有军事行动领域中作战的战备部队。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 朱尼·费舍尔（Journey Fisher）拍摄）

2026年8月21日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近印度尼西亚海军陆战队第9营举行的排级交流活动中，美国海军陆战队“达尔文轮换部队26”第5海军陆战团第1营A连班长 Sgt. 詹姆斯·马丁（James Martin）在实弹射击场使用 M4 卡宾枪射击。今年的年度排级交流在 MRF-D 与印度尼西亚武装部队第4旅第7步兵营之间进行，旨在提升联合战斗战备、强化战术互操作性，并巩固两国之间持久的伙伴关系。马丁是加利福尼亚州人。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

2026年8月22日，在南卡罗来纳州帕里斯岛海军陆战队新兵训练基地，美国海军陆战队新兵训练团支援营 Sierra 连高级操练教官 Sgt. 布兰登·安东尼（Brandon Anthony）在“接收”环节等待向系列指挥官报到。“接收”是指新兵与教官见面的环节，这些教官将负责在为期13周的新兵训练期间对他们进行训练和指导。（美国海军陆战队 Cpl. 乔迪·莫拉莱斯（Jordy Morales）摄）

2026年8月31日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近的印度尼西亚海军陆战队第7步兵营基地举行的“超级加鲁达之盾26”演习开幕式上，美国海军陆战队“达尔文轮换部队26”第5海军陆战团第1营A连的陆战队员、印度尼西亚海军陆战队第4步兵旅第7步兵营的陆战队员、韩国海军陆战队第6陆战旅第3侦察营的陆战队员以及日本陆上自卫队水陆机动团第2水陆机动连队的队员立正站立。“超级加鲁达之盾”是印度尼西亚国民军与美军之间的年度演习，旨在加强双边互操作性、能力与合作。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

items.title: DAF leaders, their spouses highlight families’ role in mission success
items.author: Tech. Sgt. William A. O’Brien
items.summary: Top leaders of the Air Force and Space Force, joined by their spouses, offered observations into the lives of military families and how that dynamic contributes in real ways to readiness and defense of the nation.
items.body:
A U.S. Marine Corps KC-130J Super Hercules pilot with Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 352, Marine Aircraft Group (MAG) 11, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing observes his surroundings while flying above California, Oct. 17, 2022. The KC-130 is a multi-role, multi-mission tactical tanker and transport aircraft which provides in-flight refueling to fixed wing, rotary wing, and tiltrotor aircraft, as well as rapid ground refueling when required. MAG 11 generates, embarks, and integrates relevant, combat ready aviation forces capable of providing Offensive Air Support, Anti-Aircraft Warfare, Assault Support, Aerial Reconnaissance, and terminal area Control of Aircraft, all in order to ensure success in combat in support of the Marine Air-Ground Task Force and Combatant Commanders. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Jackson Rush)

U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Felix Lopez, a parachute rigger deployed with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, pilots a PS-2 parachute during bilateral free-fall operations in Bizerte, Tunisia, Sept. 21, 2026. This military free-fall training enhanced airborne crisis-response capabilities and reinforced our enduring security partnership with Tunisia to strengthen collaborative cooperation and increase operational readiness with the African nation. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Isaac Garza)

U.S. Marines with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, and Tunisian Special Operations Maritime Task Group members fast-rope from a Tunisian UH-60M Black Hawk for visit, board, search and seizure training during exercise Phoenix Express 2026 in Bizerte, Tunisia, Sept. 16, 2026. Phoenix Express 2026 is a multinational maritime exercise sponsored by U.S. Africa Command and led by U.S. 6th Fleet under U.S. Naval Forces Africa, bringing together North African, European and U.S. maritime forces as part of a global network of navies to enhance cooperation and expertise in maritime security operations in the southern Mediterranean Sea. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Noah Masog)

The Mobile All-Domain Observation and Sensing System (MA-DOSS) prototype supports Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 in coordination with the Provost Marshall’s Office Aug. 19, 2026, during a live-fire exercise. This new capability quietly demonstrated how the Marine Corps is adapting the rules of expeditionary force protection. (PAE Marine Corps photo by Helena Yared)

U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Jerron Cly, a rifleman assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, prepares to fire a multi-role, anti-armor, anti-personnel, weapon system during a heavy explosive weapons range for a live-fire basic skills package at Marine Corps Base Hawaii, Sept. 2, 2026. The live-fire training focused on combat readiness and small-unit leadership through long and short-bay drills, fragmentation grenade employment, and a heavy explosive weapons package, developing 3rd LCT’s team leaders’ ability to employ Marines and make sound decisions in a dynamic combat environment. Cly is from New Mexico. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Iyer Ramakrishna)

MARINE CORPS AIR GROUND COMBAT CENTER TWENTYNINE PALMS, Calif. - During a live-fire exercise in support of Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 in coordination with the Provost Marshal’s Office Aug. 19, 2026, a new capability quietly demonstrated how the Marine Corps is adapting the rules of expeditionary force protection.

U.S. Marines with 3rd Battalion, 2nd Marines, Littoral Combat Force 24, fire a M224 60mm mortar system during a live-fire range at Camp Santiago Joint Training Center, Puerto Rico, Sept. 2, 2026. U.S. military forces are deployed to the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility in support of Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere, Department of War-directed operations, and the President's priorities to disrupt illicit drug trafficking, deter malign actors and protect the homeland through continuous presence. (U.S. Marine Corps photo)

U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. James Brooks, an infantry rifleman, and U.S. Navy Petty Officer 3rd Class Valeria Carmona, a hospital corpsman, both with the 1st Battalion, 6th Marine Regiment, 2nd Marine Division, assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border (JTF-SB) in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, pose for a photo after being awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal near Campo, California, Aug. 15, 2026. Brooks and Carmona were presented with the award for saving the life of an suspected illegal alien that was suffering from a heat-related illness. U.S. Northern Command is working side-by-side with the Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection within narrowly defined authorities to provide unique military capabilities to protect the territorial integrity of the U.S. southern border. (Dept. of War photo by Sgt. Nathan Hislop)

A Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal sits on the collar of U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. James Brooks, an infantry rifleman, with the 1st Battalion, 6th Marine Regiment, 2nd Marine Division, assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border (JTF-SB) in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, the medal was presented during an award ceremony near Campo, California, Aug. 15, 2026. Brooks was presented with the award for saving the life of a suspected illegal alien that was suffering from a heat-related illness. U.S. Northern Command is working side-by-side with the Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection within narrowly defined authorities to provide unique military capabilities to protect the territorial integrity of the U.S. southern border. (Dept. of War photo by Sgt. Nathan Hislop)

U.S. Marines with Golf Company, 2nd Battalion, 1st Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, fire an M3E1 multipurpose anti-armor anti-personnel weapon system during a platoon-level urban assault as part of Service Level Training Exercise 4-26 at Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, California, Sept. 1, 2026. SLTE is designed to be a challenging, realistic training exercise that produces combat-ready forces capable of operating as an integrated Marine Air-Ground Task Force across all domains of military operations. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Vincent Needham)

U.S. Marine Corps light armored vehicles assigned to the 4th Light Armored Reconnaissance Battalion, 4th Marine Division, Marine Forces Reserve, conduct a convoy during a Reserve Mobilization Exercise, Maryland, June 29, 2026. The week-long exercise validates the battalion's ability to rapidly activate personnel and equipment, ensuring the unit can deliver ready forces in response to a national crisis.

A U.S. Marine with Maritime Raid Force, 26th Marine Expeditionary Unit, parachutes into a drop zone during a military freefall sustainment at Raeford, North Carolina, Sept. 3, 2026. Military freefall sustainments are necessary to conduct parachute operations in support of the 26th MEU’s upcoming deployment. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Osmar VasquezHernandez)

U.S. Marines assigned to 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, detect and track simulated adversary forces during a sensing expeditionary advanced base training mission at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, Aug. 22, 2026. The 13th MEU and the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group are underway and conducting routine operations in the U.S. 3rd Fleet area of operations to enhance their combined Navy-Marine Corps readiness and lethality. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Martha Linares)

A U.S. Marine Corps MV-22B Osprey assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced), 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, transits to the forward arming and refueling point at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, Aug. 22, 2026. The 13th MEU and the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group are underway and conducting routine operations in the U.S. 3rd Fleet area of operations to enhance their combined Navy-Marine Corps readiness and lethality. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Martha Linares)

U.S. Marine Corps Joint Light Tactical Vehicles, a Strikemaster mobile anti-ship missile system, and a Norwegian Army National Manoeuvre Air Defence System displace across austere terrain while under tactical escort by Norwegian Home Guard soldiers with 3rd Platoon, District 11, in Jan Mayen, Norway, Aug. 30, 2026. The displacement and interoperability assessment, conducted during Operation Atlantic City 26, evaluated combined command, control, and multi-domain connectivity to ensure NATO can rapidly coordinate layered fires and air defense across contested environments in the High North. Atlantic City 26 is a Norwegian-led trilateral readiness initiative with the United Kingdom and United States designed to develop and demonstrate expeditionary advanced base capabilities and validate combined fires, maritime domain awareness, and sea denial to reinforce the security and stability of the High North. Jan Mayen is sovereign Norwegian territory in an isolated part of the Norwegian Sea, approximately 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from mainland Norway. At the same time, the island occupies an important geostrategic position north of the Greenland-Iceland-U.K. gap, an area of water strategically significant to the defense of the U.S. homeland and northern Europe. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Noah Masog)

U.S. Marines with Echo Company, 2nd Battalion, 1st Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, maneuver to a building during a platoon-level urban assault as part of Service Level Training 4-26 at Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, California, Aug. 30, 2026. SLTE is designed to be a challenging, realistic training exercise that produces combat-ready forces capable of operating as an integrated Marine Air-Ground Task Force across all domains of military operations. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl. Journey Fisher)

U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. James Martin, a squad leader with Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, fires an M4 carbine during a live-fire range as part of a platoon exchange at the Indonesian Marine Corps 9th Battalion near Lampung, Indonesia, Aug. 21, 2026. This year’s iteration of the annual platoon exchange is between MRF-D and the Indonesian Armed Forces 7th Infantry Battalion, 4th Brigade, designed to enhance combined combat readiness, strengthen tactical interoperability, and reinforce the enduring partnership between both nations. Martin is a native of California. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Kyle Chan)

U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Brandon Anthony, a senior drill instructor with Sierra Company, Support Battalion, Recruit Training Regiment, waits to report to the series commander during pick up on Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, S.C., Aug. 22, 2026. Pick up is when recruits meet the drill instructors who will be responsible for training and mentoring them during the 13-week recruit training. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Jordy Morales)

U.S. Marines with Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, Indonesian marines with 7th Infantry Battalion, 4th Infantry Brigade, Republic of Korea marines with 3rd Reconnaissance Battalion, 6th Marine Brigade, and Japan Ground Self-Defense Force service members with 2nd Amphibious Rapid Deployment Regiment, Amphibious Rapid Deployment Brigade, stand at attention during an opening ceremony for Exercise Super Garuda Shield 26 at the Indonesian Marine Corps 7th Infantry Battalion base near Lampung, Indonesia, Aug. 31, 2026. Super Garuda Shield is an annual exercise between the Indonesian National Armed Forces and U.S. Military designed to strengthen bilateral interoperability, capabilities, and cooperation. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Kyle Chan)

zhParas: 美国海军陆战队第3海军陆战队航空联队海军陆战队航空大队（MAG）11下属海军陆战队空中加油运输中队（VMGR）352的一名KC-130J“超级大力神”飞行员，于2022年10月17日在加利福尼亚上空飞行时观察周围情况。KC-130是一种多用途、多任务战术加油运输机，可为固定翼、旋翼和倾转旋翼飞机提供空中加油，并可在需要时快速进行地面加油。MAG 11负责生成、搭载并整合相关且具备战备状态的航空力量，能够提供进攻性空中支援、防空作战、突击支援、空中侦察以及终端区飞机控制，以确保在支援海军陆战队空地特遣部队和作战司令部司令时取得战斗胜利。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 杰克逊·拉什（Jackson Rush）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队 Staff Sgt. 费利克斯·洛佩斯（Felix Lopez）是一名降落伞检修员，随第2海军陆战师第2侦察营部队侦察连部署。2026年9月21日，他在突尼斯比塞大举行的双边自由落体行动中操纵PS-2降落伞。此次军事自由落体训练增强了空中危机响应能力，并巩固了美国与突尼斯持久的安全伙伴关系，以加强与这个非洲国家的协作配合并提高行动战备。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 艾萨克·加尔萨（Isaac Garza）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第2海军陆战师第2侦察营部队侦察连的海军陆战队员与突尼斯特种作战海上任务组成员，于2026年9月16日在突尼斯比塞大举行的“凤凰快车2026”演习中，从一架突尼斯UH-60M Black Hawk上快速滑降，进行登临、检查、搜索和扣押训练。“凤凰快车2026”是由美国非洲司令部主办、美国海军非洲部队下属美国第6舰队领导的多国海上演习，汇集北非、欧洲和美国海上力量，作为全球海军网络的一部分，以加强在地中海南部海上安全行动中的合作与专业技能。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 诺亚·马索格（Noah Masog）拍摄）
移动式全领域观测与传感系统（MA-DOSS）原型于2026年8月19日与宪兵主任办公室协调，在实弹演习期间支援军种级训练演习4-26。这一新能力悄然展示了海军陆战队如何调整远征部队防护规则。（PAE 海军陆战队照片，由 海伦娜·亚雷德（Helena Yared）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队 Lance Cpl. 杰伦·克莱（Jerron Cly）是第3海军陆战师第3海军陆战滨海团第3滨海战斗队的一名步枪手。2026年9月2日，在夏威夷海军陆战队基地举行的实弹基本技能包训练中，他于重型爆炸武器射击场准备发射一种多用途、反装甲、反人员武器系统。此次实弹训练通过长、短靶道演练、破片手榴弹使用和重型爆炸武器训练包，聚焦战斗战备和小队领导力，培养第3 LCT 小组长在动态战斗环境中指挥海军陆战队员并做出正确决策的能力。克莱来自新墨西哥州。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 伊耶尔·拉马克里希南（Iyer Ramakrishna）拍摄）
加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心——2026年8月19日，在配合宪兵主任办公室、支援军种级训练演习4-26的实弹演习期间，一项新能力悄然展示了海军陆战队如何调整远征部队防护规则。
美国海军陆战队第2陆战团第3营、滨海战斗部队24的海军陆战队员，于2026年9月2日在波多黎各圣地亚哥营联合训练中心实弹靶场发射M224 60mm迫击炮系统。美军部队部署至美国南方司令部责任区，支援西半球联合特遣部队、战争部指导的行动以及总统的优先事项，即通过持续存在打击非法毒品贩运、威慑恶意行为者并保护本土。（美国海军陆战队照片）

美国海军陆战队 Lance Cpl. 詹姆斯·布鲁克斯（James Brooks）是一名步兵步枪手，美国海军 Petty Officer 3rd Class 瓦莱里娅·卡莫纳（Valeria Carmona）是一名医务兵，两人均隶属于第2海军陆战师第6海军陆战团第1营，被派往南部边境联合特遣部队（JTF-SB），支援“热忱先锋”行动。2026年8月15日，在加利福尼亚州坎波附近，布鲁克斯和卡莫纳在获颁海军与海军陆战队成就奖章后合影。两人因救下一名患热相关疾病的疑似非法外国人而获颁该奖章。美国北方司令部正与国土安全部和美国海关与边境保护局在严格界定的权限内并肩合作，提供独特的军事能力，以保护美国南部边境的领土完整。（战争部照片，由 Sgt. 内森·希斯洛普（Nathan Hislop）拍摄）

一枚海军与海军陆战队成就奖章佩戴在美国海军陆战队 Lance Cpl. 詹姆斯·布鲁克斯（James Brooks）的衣领上。布鲁克斯是海军陆战队第2师第6陆战团第1营的一名步兵步枪手，配属南方边境联合特遣部队（JTF-SB），支援“热忱先锋”行动（Operation Ardent Vanguard）。该奖章于2026年8月15日在加利福尼亚州坎波附近举行的颁奖仪式上颁发。布鲁克斯因救下一名患热相关疾病的疑似非法入境者而获此奖章。美军北方司令部正与国土安全部及美国海关与边境保护局在严格界定的权限范围内并肩协作，提供独特的军事能力，以保护美国南部边境的领土完整。（战争部照片，由 Sgt. 内森·希斯洛普（Nathan Hislop）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第1师第1陆战团第2营G连的海军陆战队员，2026年9月1日在加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心，作为“军种级训练演习4-26”（Service Level Training Exercise 4-26）的一部分，在排级城市突击中发射一具M3E1多用途反装甲反人员武器系统。SLTE 旨在成为一项富有挑战性、贴近实战的训练演习，以打造能够作为一体化海军陆战队空地特遣部队在所有军事行动领域作战的、具备战斗力的部队。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 文森特·尼达姆（Vincent Needham）拍摄）
配属海军陆战队预备队第4陆战师第4轻型装甲侦察营的美国海军陆战队轻型装甲车，2026年6月29日在马里兰州举行的预备队动员演习中实施车队机动。这场为期一周的演习检验了该营快速动员人员与装备的能力，确保该部队能够响应国家危机，投送随时可用的部队。
美国海军陆战队第26海军陆战队远征分队海上突击部队的一名海军陆战队员，2026年9月3日在北卡罗来纳州雷福德举行的军事自由落体保持训练中跳伞进入空降场。军事自由落体保持训练是执行伞降行动、支援第26海军陆战队远征分队即将进行的部署所必需的。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Cpl. 奥斯马尔·巴斯克斯-埃尔南德斯（Osmar VasquezHernandez）拍摄）
配属第13海军陆战队远征分队的美国海军陆战队员，2026年8月22日在加利福尼亚州彭德尔顿海军陆战队基地举行的感知远征前进基地训练任务中，探测并跟踪模拟敌军部队。第13海军陆战队远征分队与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升其海军—海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

一架配属第13海军陆战队远征分队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队（VMM）364（加强）的美国海军陆战队 MV-22B“鱼鹰”倾转旋翼机，2026年8月22日飞往加利福尼亚州彭德尔顿海军陆战队基地的前沿武装加油点。第13海军陆战队远征分队与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升其海军—海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队联合轻型战术车、一套 Strikemaster 机动反舰导弹系统以及一套挪威陆军国家机动防空系统，2026年8月30日在挪威扬马延，于挪威国民警卫队第11区第3排士兵的战术护送下穿越荒芜地形实施转移。这项在“大西洋城26”行动（Operation Atlantic City 26）期间实施的转移与互操作性评估，检验了联合指挥、控制与多域互联互通能力，以确保北约能够在高北地区的争议环境中快速协调分层火力与防空。“大西洋城26”是由挪威主导，英国与美国参与的三边战备倡议，旨在发展和展示远征前进基地能力，并验证联合火力、海上态势感知与海上拒止能力，以强化高北地区的安全与稳定。扬马延是挪威的主权领土，位于挪威海一处偏远海域，距挪威大陆约1,000公里（620英里）。与此同时，该岛地处格陵兰—冰岛—英国缺口以北的重要地缘战略位置，这片水域对美国本土及北欧的防御具有重要战略意义。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 诺亚·马索格（Noah Masog）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第1师第1陆战团第2营E连的海军陆战队员，2026年8月30日在加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心，作为“军种级训练4-26”的一部分，在排级城市突击中向一栋建筑机动。SLTE 旨在成为一项富有挑战性、贴近实战的训练演习，以打造能够作为一体化海军陆战队空地特遣部队在所有军事行动领域作战的、具备战斗力的部队。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 朱尼·费舍尔（Journey Fisher）拍摄）

2026年8月21日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近的印尼海军陆战队第9营，作为排级交流活动的一部分，美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 詹姆斯·马丁（James Martin）在实弹射击场使用 M4 卡宾枪射击。马丁是海军陆战队达尔文轮换部队26（Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26）第5陆战团第1营A连的班长。今年这一年度排级交流活动在达尔文轮换部队与印尼武装部队第4旅第7步兵营之间展开，旨在提升联合战斗战备水平、增强战术互操作性，并巩固两国持久的伙伴关系。马丁原籍加利福尼亚州。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）
2026年8月22日，在南卡罗来纳州帕里斯岛海军陆战队新兵训练基地，美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 布兰登·安东尼（Brandon Anthony）在接收日等待向序列指挥官报到。他是新兵训练团支援营Sierra连的高级操练教官。接收日是新兵与操练教官见面的日子，这些教官将负责在为期13周的新兵训练期间对他们进行训练和指导。（美国海军陆战队 Cpl. 乔迪·莫拉莱斯（Jordy Morales）摄）

2026年8月31日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近的印尼海军陆战队第7步兵营基地，美国海军陆战队达尔文轮换部队26第5陆战团第1营A连的陆战队员、印尼海军陆战队第4步兵旅第7步兵营的陆战队员、韩国海军陆战队第6陆战旅第3侦察营的陆战队员，以及日本陆上自卫队水陆机动团第2水陆机动连队的官兵，在“超级神鹰之盾26”演习开幕式上立正列队。超级神鹰之盾是印度尼西亚国民军与美国军队之间的年度演习，旨在加强双边互操作性、能力与合作。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

美国海军陆战队第3海军陆战队航空联队海军陆战队航空大队（MAG）11下属海军陆战队空中加油运输中队（VMGR）352的一名KC-130J“超级大力神”飞行员，于2022年10月17日在加利福尼亚上空飞行时观察周围情况。KC-130是一种多用途、多任务战术加油运输机，可为固定翼、旋翼和倾转旋翼飞机提供空中加油，并可在需要时快速进行地面加油。MAG 11负责生成、搭载并整合相关且具备战备状态的航空力量，能够提供进攻性空中支援、防空作战、突击支援、空中侦察以及终端区飞机控制，以确保在支援海军陆战队空地特遣部队和作战司令部司令时取得战斗胜利。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 杰克逊·拉什（Jackson Rush）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队 Staff Sgt. 费利克斯·洛佩斯（Felix Lopez）是一名降落伞检修员，随第2海军陆战师第2侦察营部队侦察连部署。2026年9月21日，他在突尼斯比塞大举行的双边自由落体行动中操纵PS-2降落伞。此次军事自由落体训练增强了空中危机响应能力，并巩固了美国与突尼斯持久的安全伙伴关系，以加强与这个非洲国家的协作配合并提高行动战备。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 艾萨克·加尔萨（Isaac Garza）拍摄）

移动式全领域观测与传感系统（MA-DOSS）原型于2026年8月19日与宪兵主任办公室协调，在实弹演习期间支援军种级训练演习4-26。这一新能力悄然展示了海军陆战队如何调整远征部队防护规则。（PAE 海军陆战队照片，由 海伦娜·亚雷德（Helena Yared）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队 Lance Cpl. 杰伦·克莱（Jerron Cly）是第3海军陆战师第3海军陆战滨海团第3滨海战斗队的一名步枪手。2026年9月2日，在夏威夷海军陆战队基地举行的实弹基本技能包训练中，他于重型爆炸武器射击场准备发射一种多用途、反装甲、反人员武器系统。此次实弹训练通过长、短靶道演练、破片手榴弹使用和重型爆炸武器训练包，聚焦战斗战备和小队领导力，培养第3 LCT 小组长在动态战斗环境中指挥海军陆战队员并做出正确决策的能力。克莱来自新墨西哥州。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 伊耶尔·拉马克里希南（Iyer Ramakrishna）拍摄）

配属海军陆战队预备队第4陆战师第4轻型装甲侦察营的美国海军陆战队轻型装甲车，2026年6月29日在马里兰州举行的预备队动员演习中实施车队机动。这场为期一周的演习检验了该营快速动员人员与装备的能力，确保该部队能够响应国家危机，投送随时可用的部队。

美国海军陆战队第26海军陆战队远征分队海上突击部队的一名海军陆战队员，2026年9月3日在北卡罗来纳州雷福德举行的军事自由落体保持训练中跳伞进入空降场。军事自由落体保持训练是执行伞降行动、支援第26海军陆战队远征分队即将进行的部署所必需的。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Cpl. 奥斯马尔·巴斯克斯-埃尔南德斯（Osmar VasquezHernandez）拍摄）

配属第13海军陆战队远征分队的美国海军陆战队员，2026年8月22日在加利福尼亚州彭德尔顿海军陆战队基地举行的感知远征前进基地训练任务中，探测并跟踪模拟敌军部队。第13海军陆战队远征分队与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升其海军—海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

一架配属第13海军陆战队远征分队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队（VMM）364（加强）的美国海军陆战队 MV-22B“鱼鹰”倾转旋翼机，2026年8月22日飞往加利福尼亚州彭德尔顿海军陆战队基地的前沿武装加油点。第13海军陆战队远征分队与马金岛号两栖戒备群正在海上航行，并在美国第3舰队作战区域内执行例行行动，以提升其海军—海军陆战队联合战备水平与杀伤力。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 玛莎·利纳雷斯（Martha Linares）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队联合轻型战术车、一套 Strikemaster 机动反舰导弹系统以及一套挪威陆军国家机动防空系统，2026年8月30日在挪威扬马延，于挪威国民警卫队第11区第3排士兵的战术护送下穿越荒芜地形实施转移。这项在“大西洋城26”行动（Operation Atlantic City 26）期间实施的转移与互操作性评估，检验了联合指挥、控制与多域互联互通能力，以确保北约能够在高北地区的争议环境中快速协调分层火力与防空。“大西洋城26”是由挪威主导，英国与美国参与的三边战备倡议，旨在发展和展示远征前进基地能力，并验证联合火力、海上态势感知与海上拒止能力，以强化高北地区的安全与稳定。扬马延是挪威的主权领土，位于挪威海一处偏远海域，距挪威大陆约1,000公里（620英里）。与此同时，该岛地处格陵兰—冰岛—英国缺口以北的重要地缘战略位置，这片水域对美国本土及北欧的防御具有重要战略意义。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Sgt. 诺亚·马索格（Noah Masog）拍摄）

美国海军陆战队第1师第1陆战团第2营E连的海军陆战队员，2026年8月30日在加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村海军陆战队空地作战中心，作为“军种级训练4-26”的一部分，在排级城市突击中向一栋建筑机动。SLTE 旨在成为一项富有挑战性、贴近实战的训练演习，以打造能够作为一体化海军陆战队空地特遣部队在所有军事行动领域作战的、具备战斗力的部队。（美国海军陆战队照片，由 Lance Cpl. 朱尼·费舍尔（Journey Fisher）拍摄）

2026年8月21日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近的印尼海军陆战队第9营，作为排级交流活动的一部分，美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 詹姆斯·马丁（James Martin）在实弹射击场使用 M4 卡宾枪射击。马丁是海军陆战队达尔文轮换部队26（Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26）第5陆战团第1营A连的班长。今年这一年度排级交流活动在达尔文轮换部队与印尼武装部队第4旅第7步兵营之间展开，旨在提升联合战斗战备水平、增强战术互操作性，并巩固两国持久的伙伴关系。马丁原籍加利福尼亚州。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

2026年8月22日，在南卡罗来纳州帕里斯岛海军陆战队新兵训练基地，美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 布兰登·安东尼（Brandon Anthony）在接收日等待向序列指挥官报到。他是新兵训练团支援营Sierra连的高级操练教官。接收日是新兵与操练教官见面的日子，这些教官将负责在为期13周的新兵训练期间对他们进行训练和指导。（美国海军陆战队 Cpl. 乔迪·莫拉莱斯（Jordy Morales）摄）

2026年8月31日，在印度尼西亚楠榜附近的印尼海军陆战队第7步兵营基地，美国海军陆战队达尔文轮换部队26第5陆战团第1营A连的陆战队员、印尼海军陆战队第4步兵旅第7步兵营的陆战队员、韩国海军陆战队第6陆战旅第3侦察营的陆战队员，以及日本陆上自卫队水陆机动团第2水陆机动连队的官兵，在“超级神鹰之盾26”演习开幕式上立正列队。超级神鹰之盾是印度尼西亚国民军与美国军队之间的年度演习，旨在加强双边互操作性、能力与合作。（美国海军陆战队 Sgt. 凯尔·陈（Kyle Chan）摄）

Military low flying: RAF operational low flying training timetable

Royal Air Force (RAF) operational low flying training timetables in 3 areas of the UK.

Ministry of Defence

1 August 2011

23 September 2026 — See all updates

Operational Low Flying Training Timetable 21 September to 25 September 2026

Operational Low Flying Training Timetable 28 September to 2 October 2026

Operational Low Flying Training Timetable 5 to 9 October 2026

Timetables for operational low flying ( OLF ) training by RAF fast jets and Hercules aircraft. These timetables cover 3 tactical training areas ( TTA ) only. These are:

LFA 7(T): central Wales

LFA 14(T): northern Scotland

LFA 20(T): the borders of southern Scotland and northern England

When the TTA is not in use, there may be other flying activity in the area. The MOD is unable to provide a timetable for all low flying activity as the information can very quickly become outdated due to weather conditions and training requirements.

Other low flying schedules

Military low flying: MOD sponsored air exercises

Military low flying: air weapons ranges activity

Low flying military aircraft includes information about how to contact MOD about low flying in your area

Military low flying includes detailed information about why we carry out low flying in the UK

items.title: German defense minister sees smooth sailing in parliament for his record defense budget
items.author: Linus Höller
items.summary: Pistorius is asking lawmakers to approve nearly €140 billion ($160 billion) for defense next year, a record sum.
items.body:
VIENNA — German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius told reporters after a Bundestag defense committee hearing on Wednesday that lawmakers had shown “much agreement” on his ministry’s record 2027 budget request, even as he pushed back against criticism that Germany is buying too much legacy hardware rather than new technology.

Pistorius is asking parliament to approve nearly €140 billion ($160 billion) for defense next year, combining €109.7 billion from the core ministry budget — a 32.7% increase over 2026 — with roughly €30 billion drawn from the expiring Sondervermögen Bundeswehr, a special off-budget fund created in 2022 following Russia’s attack on Ukraine.

The committee session Wednesday was part of ongoing scrutiny before the Bundestag’s final vote, expected in the chamber’s third reading on Nov. 27, following a reconciliation session in the budget committee on November 12.

Speaking after the closed-door meeting, Pistorius rejected accusations — raised by some lawmakers and commentators — that the procurement plan favors old technology over modernization. He pointed to the Leopard 2A8 tank as a “high-tech” system rather than legacy equipment, and announced that the ministry will launch its first-ever dedicated funding program for civilian universities and research institutes working on defense-relevant technologies, including artificial intelligence and unmanned systems.

On the Franco-German Main Ground Combat System, Pistorius acknowledged that the program’s original design may not survive in its current form. A day earlier, Germany and France had published a joint announcement that the project would be transitioned to pursuing “platform-independent technology” rather than a main battle tank. Pistorius said Berlin and Paris would need to agree “in the coming weeks” on shifting toward “a different, restructured project” given a threat environment he described as markedly changed from four or five years ago. The joint next-generation tank concept traces back all the way to 2012.

Despite unified opposition from the right-wing AfD, the Greens and far-left Die Linke — who call the spending plan fiscally reckless or insufficiently transparent — the governing coalition holds the votes needed to pass the budget.

Linus Höller is Defense News' Europe correspondent and OSINT investigator. He reports on the arms deals, sanctions, and geopolitics shaping Europe and the world. He holds master’s degrees in WMD nonproliferation, terrorism studies, and international relations, and works in four languages: English, German, Russian, and Spanish.
zhParas: 维也纳——德国国防部长鲍里斯·皮斯托里乌斯（Boris Pistorius）周三在联邦议院国防委员会听证会后告诉记者，议员们对其部门创纪录的2027年预算请求表现出“很大共识”，同时他反驳了有关德国购买过多旧式硬件而非新技术的批评。
皮斯托里乌斯正请求议会批准明年近1400亿欧元（1600亿美元）的国防预算，其中包括来自该部核心预算的1097亿欧元——较2026年增长32.7%——以及从即将到期的“联邦国防军特别基金”（Sondervermögen Bundeswehr）中提取的约300亿欧元；该基金是2022年俄罗斯袭击乌克兰后设立的预算外特别基金。
周三的委员会会议是联邦议院最终投票前持续审查的一部分；最终投票预计于11月27日在议院三读中进行，此前预算委员会已于11月12日举行协调会议。
在闭门会议后发言时，皮斯托里乌斯驳斥了一些议员和评论人士提出的指控，即采购计划偏向旧技术而非现代化。他指出，Leopard 2A8坦克是“高科技”系统，而非遗留装备，并宣布该部将启动其有史以来首个专项资助计划，面向从事国防相关技术（包括人工智能和无人系统）研究的民用大学和研究机构。

关于法德“主要地面作战系统”（Main Ground Combat System），皮斯托里乌斯承认该项目的原始设计可能无法以当前形式存续。一天前，德国和法国发布联合声明称，该项目将转向追求“平台无关技术”，而非主战坦克。皮斯托里乌斯表示，鉴于他形容为与四五年前明显不同的威胁环境，柏林和巴黎需要“在未来几周内”就转向“一个不同且经重组调整的项目”达成一致。这一联合下一代坦克概念可追溯至2012年。
尽管右翼的德国选择党（AfD）、绿党和极左翼的左翼党（Die Linke）一致反对——他们称该支出计划在财政上鲁莽或不够透明——执政联盟仍拥有通过预算所需的票数。
利努斯·赫勒（Linus Höller）是《防务新闻》（Defense News）欧洲通讯员和开源情报（OSINT）调查员。他报道塑造欧洲和世界的军火交易、制裁和地缘政治。他拥有大规模杀伤性武器防扩散、恐怖主义研究和国际关系硕士学位，并以四种语言工作：英语、德语、俄语和西班牙语。

items.body: U.S. Marines with Expeditionary Operations Training Group, II Marine Expeditionary Force, evaluate reconnaissance Marines with the 26th Marine Expeditionary Unit and a Dutch service member on urban terrain operations during an advanced sniper course at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, Sept. 17, 2026. EOTG’s advanced sniper course is designed to train personnel in advanced combat marksmanship skills, surveillance, and communications that will support expeditionary operations necessary when forward deployed. items.author: PO1 Joseph Vazquez
items.summary: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Science Technician 2nd Class Cristian Cruz, left, a disaster management specialist assigned to Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26), speaks to participants during a natural disaster scenario-based table top exercise at a PP26 disaster management workshop in Tacloban City, Philippines, Sept. 23, 2026. The workshop, coordinated with the Philippine Office of Civil Defense, brought together personnel from various Philippine disaster response units to enhance incident command readi
items.body:
Coast Guard Marine Science Technician 2nd Class Cristian Cruz, left, a disaster management specialist assigned to Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26), speaks to participants during a natural disaster scenario-based table top exercise at a PP26 disaster management workshop in Tacloban City, Philippines, Sept.

The workshop, coordinated with the Philippine Office of Civil Defense, brought together personnel from various Philippine disaster response units to enhance incident command readiness and organization.

Now in its 22nd iteration, the Pacific Partnership series is the largest annual multinational humanitarian assistance and disaster management preparedness mission conducted in the region.

Pacific Partnership works collaboratively with host and partner nations to enhance regional interoperability and disaster response capabilities, increase security in the region, and foster new and enduring friendships in the Indo-Pacific.

Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Joseph C.
zhParas: 图中左侧的海岸警卫队二等海洋科学技师克里斯蒂安·克鲁斯（Cristian Cruz）是一名被派往“太平洋伙伴关系2026”（PP26）的灾害管理专家，9月在菲律宾塔克洛班市举行的PP26灾害管理研讨会期间，在一场基于自然灾害情景的桌面推演中向参与者讲话。
该研讨会与菲律宾民防办公室协调举办，汇集了菲律宾各灾害响应单位的人员，以提升事件指挥战备与组织。
现已举办至第22届，太平洋伙伴关系系列活动是该地区开展的规模最大的年度多国人道主义援助和灾害管理准备任务。
太平洋伙伴关系与东道国和伙伴国合作，以增强区域互操作性和灾害响应能力，增进地区安全，并在印太地区培育新的持久友谊。
美国海军照片，由海军一等大众传播专家约瑟夫·C.（Joseph C.）拍摄。

该研讨会与菲律宾民防办公室协调举办，汇集了菲律宾各灾害响应单位的人员，以提升事件指挥战备与组织。

现已举办至第22届，太平洋伙伴关系系列活动是该地区开展的规模最大的年度多国人道主义援助和灾害管理准备任务。

太平洋伙伴关系与东道国和伙伴国合作，以增强区域互操作性和灾害响应能力，增进地区安全，并在印太地区培育新的持久友谊。

Information on Dartmoor Training Area's firing times.

Ministry of Defence and Defence Infrastructure Organisation

4 July 2013

23 September 2026 — See all updates

Dartmoor six week firing times: 21 September to 1 November 2026

Do not touch any military debris it may be dangerous. Please note the location and inform a Training Safety Officer (TSO) or police.

Warning signals: red flags by day and red lamps by night, indicate that live firing is taking place within the range boundaries, which are marked by red and white poles. When warning signals are displayed do not cross the range boundary.

items.title: Europe’s push to reduce US reliance is reshaping the defense space market
items.author: Rudy Ruitenberg
items.summary: Spooked by U.S. restrictions on satellite data access during recent crises, European countries are scrambling to catch up on sovereign capabilities.
items.body:
PARIS — Demand for sovereign satellite capabilities is growing in Europe as governments seek greater control over access to relevant infrastructure.

The push comes after restrictions by the United States on satellite access in Ukraine and the Middle East over the past two years underscored the risk of dependence, executives and policy makers said at an industry conference here last week.

“Sovereignty” was a recurring theme at the World Space Business Week, held from Sept. 14 to 17 in Paris, and the two-day Space Defense & Security Summit side event.

U.S. firms touted their ability to build satellites in Europe or operate free from International Traffic in Arms Regulations, while European companies highlighted their ability to provide local clients with complete satellite systems.

“The drive to sovereignty, we all have customers that want to go there,” said Noam Segal, the chief executive officer of Israeli firm ImageSat International, or ISI. “Any of the defense customers we are dealing with can find themselves in a geopolitical situation in which one of the suppliers will not be able to deliver. I think this is the driver.”

The war in Ukraine has highlighted both the importance of satellite data on the modern battlefield and the reliance of Western militaries on U.S. suppliers for critical space capabilities. Restrictions on Starlink access in Ukraine, a halt in U.S. intelligence sharing with Ukraine in March 2025 and imagery restrictions over the Middle East in 2026 are pushing European countries to seek sovereign alternatives.

The lesson from Ukraine has been to show how critical space has become for defense, as well as “the importance of indeed not being reliant on solutions you don’t control,” said Guillaume de la Brosse, head of the defense policy and innovation unit at the European Commission, the European Union’s executive arm.

He said there is a “clear imperative” to accelerate development of sovereign space-based capabilities in Europe, meaning a minimum backbone of public assets owned by either the EU or member states, and an EU-based industry able to provide sovereign services “that we can control all the time.”

“Sovereignty very much matters, this is what we’ve learned from Ukraine,” De la Brosse said. “That does not preclude the fact that we need cooperation, whatever happens, but that as a pre-requirement has sovereignty. It’s good to cut dependencies where we need to cut dependencies, and that’s very much the agenda of the upcoming years.”

Recent history showed space sovereignty is the only ultimate guarantee of having the freedom to “assess and act when conflict breaks out,” said Jean-Baptiste Paing, a deputy director at France’s Directorate General for Armament whose responsibilities include intelligence and space operations. He cited the difficulty obtaining commercial satellite communications over Afghanistan and, more recently, access to commercial imaging during the various crises in the Middle East.

The emergence of New Space, the shift from a government-dominated to a private space industry that has cut the cost of launchers and satellites, is allowing European governments to establish space sovereignty even with relatively limited budgets, executives said.

The number of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance satellites for defense purposes, “a key priority for most nations,” is expected to increase more than fourfold through to 2035, according to industry consultancy Novaspace, which organized the conferences.

New Space provides “an incredible opportunity” for countries that didn’t have a space industry to develop their own sovereign capabilities, said Vincent Dedieu, the CEO of Sodern, a unit of France’s ArianeGroup. He said Sodern has been working with countries such as Poland, Bulgaria and Finland, which are taking advantage of New Space to catch up in both defense and commercial space.

The fact that customers are now able to own space assets at a “completely different cost point” from the past means the push for sovereign capabilities “is a strong trend that’s going to be there for the future,” according to Segal at ISI.

There is a “seismic shift” in how industry and governments deal with space capabilities, said Julia Gottfriedsen, chief technology officer at German thermal-imaging startup Constellr. She cited the example of Germany buying data from ICEYE and Rheinmetall for its brigade in Lithuania, through a service-level agreement that shifted the risk for data supply to the companies.

“So this is pretty modern and new, while in parallel, of course, the governments are also looking into procuring their own infrastructure,” Gottfriedsen said.

Executives at U.S.-based geospatial intelligence firms such as Planet Labs, BlackSky and Vantor all noted that their satellites can be delivered ITAR-free, with several highlighting their European presence or ability to manufacture their satellites outside the Untied States.

HawkEye 360 CEO John Serafini said partnerships with Italy’s Leonardo and Czechia’s ERA and having a Luxembourg subsidiary means he’s confident that “even as a U.S. company,” the firm can meet the requirement of European militaries “regardless of how those customers want the sovereignty delivered to them.”

Planet Labs cut the ribbon on a new facility in Berlin this week, and co-Founder and Chief Strategy Officer Robbie Schingler said the company’s first German-built Pelican satellite is set to come off the production line by the end of the year and sent into orbit on a German-built Isar Aerospace rocket launched from Norway “sometime early next year.”

Meanwhile, Finland’s ICEYE is taking sovereignty “to a whole different level” to fulfill a German order for a 40-satellite constellation, setting up a manufacturing site in western Germany controlled by a German-owned entity and keeping the entire supply chain within the country, according to CEO Rafal Modrzewski. That does require a sufficiently large order to justify the investment, he said.

For European customers that own and operate a smaller number of ICEYE satellites, such as Sweden, Finland, Poland and the Netherlands, the company is now offering a software layer that allows countries to “federate their assets at the tactical level” and borrow each other’s capabilities to cover areas of interest, Modrzewski said.

One element of sovereignty is assurance and control, another is choice, said Schingler at Planet Labs. The federation approach allows countries to network their systems for an ad hoc mission, “and that choice also gives a lot of sovereignty,” he said.

The European Commission is pushing for international cooperation to remain the way of doing things in space, including through discussions with NATO about space security, even if “that cooperation is very much challenged, and there is a need for Europeans to do much more, investing in their freedom of action,” De la Brosse said.

He said that as EU members invest heavily in space, one challenge is to avoid “renationalization of space policies,” and the commission is using the EU budget to provide an incentive to member states to coordinate investments and pool space resources rather than develop constellations without taking other member states into account.

Germany’s plan to invest a “massive” €35 billion in sovereign military space capabilities by 2030 may raise concern among some EU members that the country will “fly solo,” but the investment is a legitimate sovereign choice, said Paing at the DGA.

“I cannot speak for sovereignty myself without recognizing the same capacity in other countries, and I think it should be seen more as a model to follow for others rather than something to be afraid of,” Paing said. “That being said, I believe that this investment should nevertheless be put at the service of building a stronger Europe.”

Sovereignty also includes the ability to get satellites into orbit, executives said, with several remarking on the scarcity of launch slots. Nicolas Lefort, the head of new markets at MBDA, said France’s Toutatis project to bring a maneuverable satellite into low-Earth orbit is still waiting for a launcher.

François Lombard, the head of connected intelligence at Airbus Defence and Space, said he’s optimistic about new European players offering launchers capable of carrying one-ton payloads into LEO, citing a recent successful launch by Germany’s Isar Aerospace, as well as ArianeGroup’s MaiaSpace coming to the market “pretty soon.”

“In that case, European alternatives, which is good,” Lombard said. “There are a few satellites we cannot launch from other continents, so it’s important that we have also the sovereign access to space for this class of satellites in a competitive manner.”

Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.
